results.title: [Bug]: Astra messages fail in T3 Code but the same prompt/model works in terminal Codex
Connect with ChatGPT rejects Codex subagents and leaves the chat unable to continue
[Bug]: Erroring out while launching a subagent when provider is using the "ChatGPT Sign In via sharing usage limits"

issue.title: [Bug]: Astra messages fail in T3 Code but the same prompt/model works in terminal Codex

pr.title: fix(codex): disable agents for ChatGPT sharing
pr.body:
Managed Codex sessions using Connect with ChatGPT can still expose native agent tools when the model catalog selects `multi_agent_version: "v2"`, despite the two existing disabled multi-agent feature flags. This can produce the unsupported native-agent history reported in [#17679](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/17679).

Add `agents.enabled=false` to the existing managed launch overrides. Codex checks this before catalog selection. Keep both feature flags disabled because an explicitly enabled V2 feature takes precedence over the agents switch. Ordinary local/API-key setup follows a separate path; the shared managed runtime supplies the setting to both app-server sessions and text-generation exec launches. No client or contract change is needed, including for remote clients.

Maintainer takeover of @pirut's implementation in [#20270](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/20270), preserving contributor commits and merging main. Retained the minimal two-line production change and reduced the test delta from a duplicate override parser and launch-builder assertion loop to one assertion in the existing account/executable matrix. This completes the restriction introduced in [#17499](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/17499); human approval is still outstanding.

Verification on headless Linux:

- Existing four runtime cases cover primary/additional accounts and managed/local executable selection within managed sharing. All four fail against main without the setting. No new cases or files: 5 → 5 runtime cases, and 28 → 28 passing tests across the managed-runtime, launch-argument, and Codex-driver suites. Existing main tests are preserved.
- Scoped lint, formatting, server typecheck, and whitespace checks pass.
- Installed Codex 0.163.0, isolated temporary homes, local catalog explicitly selecting agent V2, and a local scripted Responses endpoint: the original launch overrides advertised `spawn_agent`, `followup_task`, `send_message`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents`. The final overrides advertised none of those six; code execution remained available. Both fixture requests returned `OK` with exit 0. The proof uses current production override values with only provider URLs redirected locally and a dummy token; no real credentials or model inference were used.
- Independent full-diff reviews by Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Sol found no code blockers.

Screenshots do not apply to this launch-configuration change. The live check verifies CLI tool declarations rather than a complete coding/delegation/review cycle in T3. The author's original real-account success was not rerun. macOS, Windows, iOS, Android, and Electron desktop were not exercised. Existing conversations containing unsupported native-agent history are not repaired.

Closes [#21061](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/21061).

Current-head CI suites pass. Duplicate native-fingerprint cancellation has a successful replacement on the same head; it is not counted as a passing check. The PR remains unmerged for the human approval described above.

Implementation: GPT-6.1 Sol in Codex. Tests: GPT-6 Astra in Codex. Reviews: Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code and GPT-6 Sol in Codex.

comments.body:
Additional independent reproduction on Windows (2026-10-20), with a more specific rejection than the one in this issue.

**Environment**
- T3 Code 0.1.0 stable and 0.1.1-nightly.20261020.3386 (both affected)
- T3-managed Codex CLI/app-server 0.156.1
- ChatGPT subscription sharing (`modelProvider: openai_token_sharing`)
- Model `gpt-6-astra`, reasoning `medium` and `xhigh`
- awork MCP configured and working with Sol

**Minimal reproduction**: Start a new T3 Code conversation with Astra/medium and send: `Antworte ausschließlich mit OK. Verwende keine Werkzeuge.` ("Reply only OK. Do not use tools."). Reproduces even with *No project* selected, no subagent request and no tool use in the user message. The turn fails before any assistant reply, with:

```text
invalid_request_error (param: input)
code: subscription_sharing_unsupported_capability
User subscription sharing currently supports only 'web_search' and developer-defined 'function' and 'custom' tools, including 'namespace' and 'programmatic_tool_calling'; tool 'tool_search' is not supported. Remove it or use an API key instead.
```

**Controls**
- Same managed `codex.exe` (0.156.1) invoked *directly* via `codex exec --model gpt-6-astra -c 'model_reasoning_effort="medium"' --sandbox read-only --skip-git-repo-check "Antworte ausschließlich mit OK. Verwende keine Werkzeuge."` succeeds (`OK`).
- T3 Code with Sol (GPT-5.6-Sol and GPT-6-Sol) can access the awork MCP server.
- Updating T3 stable to the nightly above did not resolve the problem.

**Redacted app-server trace of the failed T3 turn (UTC)**:
```text
04:05:31.471 thread/start model=gpt-6-astra, config includes T3's local MCP server
04:05:33.910 thread created: modelProvider=openai_token_sharing
04:05:33.972 turn/start model=gpt-6-astra, effort=medium, text-only input
04:05:34.226 awork MCP ready
04:05:34.444 codex_apps and t3-code MCP ready
04:05:36.835 thread status=systemError
04:05:36.836 error: tool 'tool_search' not supported; willRetry=false
04:05:36.856 turn completed, status=failed
```

The T3 `turn/start` also includes extensive `additionalContext` orchestration instructions and `sandboxPolicy: dangerFullAccess`, unlike the direct read-only CLI control. Neither is established as causal. The log doesn't contain the full upstream Responses request, so the component that inserts `tool_search` is still unconfirmed.

**Potentially useful distinction from the original report:** here a brand-new, text-only Astra conversation fails without any observed native subagent activity. Please investigate why the T3-managed Codex app-server request advertises `tool_search` on the ChatGPT subscription-sharing route and whether that tool can be omitted for this route.

Only redacted evidence included; no raw logs, internal paths, prompts beyond the minimal reproduction, IDs, credentials or private project information.
Removed — posted from the wrong account.

## Fresh repro on current stable (0.1.5) — and evidence the #17499 fix isn't effective

Hit the exact same failure today on a brand-new thread, on the current **stable** release (not a nightly), which suggests this isn't just a lingering nightly regression.

### What happened

A new top-level Codex thread (model `gpt-6-astra`, provider `openai_token_sharing`) started a **native Codex subagent** (`subAgentActivity`, not a T3 `delegate_task`) partway through its first turn. The spawned child thread failed immediately with `subscription_sharing_unsupported_capability`; ~10s later the parent turn failed with the identical error.

### Repro sequence (UTC, from local protocol logs)

```
21:37:21.036  turn/start on parent thread (gpt-6-astra, model_provider=openai_token_sharing)
21:37:39.582  parent begins a reasoning item
21:37:42.243  parent emits item/started subAgentActivity → spawns child thread
21:37:43.782  child thread: thread/status/changed → systemError
21:37:43.783  child turn/completed, status "failed", error.code = subscription_sharing_unsupported_capability
21:37:53.305  parent thread: thread/status/changed → systemError (same error.code)
21:37:53.309  parent turn/completed, status "failed"
```

Both errors carry `"param":"input"`, `"willRetry":false`, and the same message as in the issue description ("User subscription sharing currently supports only text, image, and file messages... Remove unsupported input items or use an API key instead.").

### Why I don't think the PR #17499 fix is landing

`CodexManagedRuntime.ts` on `v0.1.5` still sets the launch overrides from that PR:

```
features.multi_agent=false
features.multi_agent_v2=false
```

But the trace above shows native `subAgentActivity` firing anyway for an `openai_token_sharing` session, on Codex CLI `0.156.1`. The PR's own verification notes flagged this gap: *"A live managed-provider request has not been verified."* That appears to be exactly what's biting here — the config override doesn't seem to actually suppress native subagent dispatch in this Codex CLI build, so the original failure mode is unchanged.

### Environment

- T3 Code server: `0.1.5` (stable)
- Codex app-server/CLI: `0.156.1`
- OS: macOS (darwin arm64)
- Auth route: Connect with ChatGPT (subscription sharing), model `gpt-6-astra`
- Desktop app + local server, both version `0.1.5`

---
Produced by Claude (Opus 4.8) via T3 Code triage (`t3 triage`).

earlier_diagnosis.body:
Still reproducing on `0.0.46-nightly.20261014.3132`. I traced why the #17499 overrides don't prevent native subagents: the model catalog takes precedence over those feature flags.

**Environment**

- T3 Code desktop `0.0.46-nightly.20261014.3132`, macOS 27.0.1 (arm64)
- Codex CLI `0.162.1`, managed provider via "Connect with ChatGPT" (`openai_token_sharing`)
- Model: `gpt-6-astra`, `ultra` reasoning

**Timeline (UTC)**

1. `05:47:45` New thread, text-only prompt.
2. `05:48:20` Parent calls `spawn_agent` (`task_name: refactor_server_domain`). The child is spawned with `gpt-6-astra` / `xhigh`.
3. `05:48:22` Child receives an `agent_message` input item (`author: /root`). At `05:48:24` the child fails with `subscription_sharing_unsupported_capability`.
4. `05:48:37` Parent spawns a second child and receives the first child's `agent_message`. At `05:48:38` the parent fails with the same error.

**Root cause**

The running app-server has `-c features.multi_agent=false -c features.multi_agent_v2=false`, and `codex features list` with those flags reports both as `false`. Native multi-agent v2 is still active because the model catalog (`models_cache.json`) sets it per model:

```text
gpt-6.1-sol   multi_agent_version=v2  multi_agent_reasoning_effort=xhigh
gpt-6-astra   multi_agent_version=v2  multi_agent_reasoning_effort=xhigh
gpt-6-sol     multi_agent_version=v2
gpt-6-luna    multi_agent_version=v2
```

In `rust-v0.162.1`, `codex-rs/core/src/config/mod.rs`:

```rust
pub(crate) fn multi_agent_version_override(&self) -> Option<MultiAgentVersion> {
    if self.features.enabled(Feature::MultiAgentV2) {
        Some(MultiAgentVersion::V2)
    } else if !self.agents_enabled {
        Some(MultiAgentVersion::Disabled)
    } else {
        None
    }
}

pub(crate) fn multi_agent_version_for_model(&self, model_multi_agent_version: Option<MultiAgentVersion>) -> MultiAgentVersion {
    self.multi_agent_version_override()
        .or(model_multi_agent_version)
        .unwrap_or_else(|| self.multi_agent_version_from_features())
}
```

Disabling the features only yields `None` from the override, so the catalog's `v2` wins. Only `agents.enabled = false` (`[agents] enabled`) returns `Disabled` ahead of the catalog. Launching the managed provider with `-c agents.enabled=false` should be the effective fix. Codex accepts the key, but I haven't verified the end-to-end behavior in T3.

The rejected input item is most likely `agent_message`: both failures happen right after an `agent_message` enters the turn input, and it isn't in the allowed list. The request body isn't logged, though.
